title: Agent Evidence Lab run ledger — v2
description: Attempt and replacement history for one preregistered study. Deliberately a SEPARATE contract from experiment_run: that schema is frozen with additionalProperties:false, and reopening a frozen data contract to record workflow history would be the wrong trade. Versioned independently because one ledger may describe runs emitted under different event-schema versions. v2.0.0 adds required traceability fields (session_id, workspace, started_at) so any run can be resolved to its transcript, its workspace and its moment without guesswork. Required rather than optional: an entry missing them is the untrackable record the ledger exists to prevent. A MAJOR bump because the requirement is breaking — no 1.0.0 ledger was ever written, so nothing is stranded.

preregistration_sha256.description: Hash of the study's frozen preregistration document as it stood when the study ran. Binds the ledger to a specific frozen protocol: a ledger cannot be carried across a preregistration change without that change being visible.

runs.description: Every attempted run, including discarded ones. Nothing is deleted.

pair_id.description: Identifies the baseline/intervention pair this run belongs to.

session_id.description: The CLIENT's session identifier — what names the transcript on disk. Distinct from run_id, which is ours. Null only when a planned run produced no session at all.

workspace.description: Absolute path the session ran in. Tier 1 only; screened out of any export, since it is a home path.

transcript_path.description: Tier 1 path to the raw transcript. Derived, stored so the lookup is not re-derived each time.

notes.description: Free-text operator note. Distinct from disposition_reason, which is the protocol's answer; this is the human's.

replacements.description: Authorised replacements only. D4 permits these solely for non-substantive execution failures; a completed_analyzable or completed_not_activated run is never replaced.

reason.description: Closed list from D4. Widening it is a further dated deviation, not a run-time judgement.

original_disposition.description: Only these may be replaced. completed_analyzable and completed_not_activated are deliberately absent from this enum, so the schema itself refuses to record a replacement the protocol forbids.
